messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Segmenting the server.r
parts:
Greetings all,

I have several concurrent apps which are mostly derivative upon one earlier prototype, and have since diverged, but many down stream portions remain the same.  Upon submission of my first completed app yesterday, today I thought it would be worth passing the updates from the down stream portions to the other apps- but that became tedious rather quickly.  So instead, I have been looking for a way to segment the server.r into modules which can be updated and applied to all apps with one file being copy/pasted, rather than going through and finding which changes were made and applying them manually.

I first tried simply putting the modules into .R files, and loading them via source(), but of course this was naive and failed.  I recalled seeing someone else do something similar, so I pulled it up.
server.r*
source("server_01.R")
source("server_02.R")

server <- function(input, output) {
  server_01(input, output)
  server_02(input, output)
}

shinyServer(server)
*
server_01.R and server_02.R were organized as*
server_02 <- function(input, output) {
  .power_gui <- 2
#normal server.r looking stuff
}
*
This seemed promising, however, the two servers did not attempt to share reactives between each other, as when I tried using this approach, the errors "function not found" popped up.  I tried including the reactives in with (input, output, reactive(), reactive2(), etc()) in the initializing functions, but the result was a different error for the unexpected (.  So my last attempt was to use the session variable, (input,output,session), but this too failed.

The next thing I was going to test was making a list object containing every single reactive, that was used in the subsequent portions, and passing that to the servers (input, output, listObject), but I wanted to ask if anyone had a better solution to this?

And as a last note, completely unrelated, I was thinking about the etymology of the name "shiny", the best I can figure is that the devs are a fan of the show Firefly, where the word shiny was used as a synonym for "cool" or a generally good thing.  Though many other television shows use the word shiny as something of interest for their dumb characters, such as Homer Simpson or The Tick.  Can you tell it's a Friday?

Thanks for your time and attention,
Mike

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: Segmenting the server.r
parts:
I have been thinking about this as well. sourcing files (directories) and addResourcePath could be part of the solution but I haven't come up with a clean solution yet. Ideally, this would extend to packages with shiny apps as well. That is, do library(base_app) and then have app components be part of another app your are running or developing. This already works for bindings but what I mean is tabs. For example, an app that handles loading/saving/plotting/summarizing/etc data would be included in an app that offers functions to process that data.

R.utils::sourceDirectory('tools/analysis', recursive = TRUE)
http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/shiny/docs/addResourcePath
